speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what is the latest assessment of transboundary haze affecting Singapore; and (b) whether bilateral and regional measures to mitigate haze are being reviewed and strengthened.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Members may wish to ask supplementary questions later and I will be happy to address them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This could result in hazy conditions affecting Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Cloud seeding for rain will not be effective, given our size and geography.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Any induced rain might not fall on Singapore due to variable wind patterns.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Regional and bilateral cooperation are therefore essential to address transboundary haze and Singapore is committed to these efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) based in Singapore provides regular updates to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states on the weather and haze situation, including hotspot information and early warnings to support their respective haze prevention and response efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singapore also engages our neighbours through platforms, such as the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) and the Ministerial Steering Committee on Transboundary Haze Pollution.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We strongly support Indonesia's efforts to operationalise the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control, to be based in Indonesia.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Centre will enhance regional preparedness and response to transboundary haze by facilitating cooperation and coordination in managing the impact of land and forest fires that cause haze pollution.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to monitor the ongoing haze situation closely.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These measures include the issuing of advisories to minimise outdoor activities and ensuring sufficient supply of N95 masks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indoor air purifiers will also be deployed in premises where vulnerable groups are likely to congregate, such as schools, public hospitals, nursing homes and polyclinics.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members of the public may stay updated through NEA's website, the MyENV app and the dedicated haze microsite at haze.gov.sg.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My question is one born out of history.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We debated in this Parliament the Transboundary Haze Pollution Bill and we saw – Mr Speaker, l will get to my point soon – a great increase in air quality.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And I think there has been a lot of cooperation from the south.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have read reports that this deluge of potential pollution came not from the south.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I would like to understand how we, as a Government, as a Ministry, is engaging the people creating this air pollution to reciprocate the domestic efforts of Singaporeans, reciprocate the domestic efforts of our Government agencies, such that, on both sides, we do not emit pollution.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And here I speak from some degree of experience.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Having done my home visits, in or around the time to my constituency, and I felt and I breathed not all that high quality of air.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I seek reciprocity in the region for all our efforts – and this is a humble request.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think we could smell it throughout Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having said that, I do share the Member's wish to see if we can, in a more effective way, go upstream and to have neighbours also paying attention to their management of air pollution.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And I would like to say that my experience in this area has shown that actually the air quality has improved.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The incidents of transboundary haze has actually reduced over the years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is in no small way, due to the efforts made by our neighbours in managing their own regulations and also their own communities domestically, but also cooperating regionally at the ASEAN level.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I would just reaffirm the suggestion of working closely with our neighbours.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We do that in a few ways: we provide information; we provide capability building; we supply forecasts regularly, quarterly, half-yearly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we see that we are getting into a potential dry season, we will step up the communications.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We even have some of the officers attached to the ASMC, so as to build up trust and also common understanding of how forecasting works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the ASEAN level, this is a constant platform for meetings and discussions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the sub-regional level, we meet up with our neighbours regularly to go through past data and also go through forecasts, so as to get everyone ready for the weather that is coming our way.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I would like to assure Members that this is really an area of focus, an area that we pay attention to and we will do our very best to get regional cooperation in managing transboundary haze.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that there is a lot of support in kind in collaborating with our cross border counterparts to tackle fire hotspots, as the Minister mentioned.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But how about some financial assistance for countries, if they require it?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, whether these have been activated recently, in view of the very dry weather and windy conditions?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As I mentioned earlier in my reply, meeting with them, the discussions on forecasting, a review of the hotspots in the past six months, 12 months, it is an ongoing process that we have with them and it is not triggered by the recent dry period.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, what I am trying to summarise is that the effort to put transboundary haze on the agenda is continuing and it has achieved its outcome because we have seen haze incidents declining over the years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having said that, we should not be complacent, because we are dealing with changing weather patterns and we expect climate change will bring about drier conditions, at the same time hotter temperatures, which make them good conditions for more potential wildfires.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I just want to assure Members that we are doing our utmost to have that discussion at the regional level.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But even with all good intentions and all good efforts by all parties involved, including our neighbours, climate change effects are being felt and we cannot rule out more wildfires contributing to haze conditions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Therefore, even as we try to manage upstream, we must also be prepared downstream to deal with hazy days when they arrive.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: If not, can the Minister share some of the challenges bringing these cases to Court?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For the first question, the answer is no.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As I have explained in my reply, we have not crossed the threshold of a haze episode, because the PSI reading has been well below 100.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to work hard to get to some conclusion on these investigations.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With the current haze persisting since late-January and doctors flagging out the elderly, children and those with pre-existing respiratory conditions as disproportionately affected, has the Inter-Agency Task Force been convened for the current episode?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And at what PSI threshold will the Government activate the distribution of N95 masks and the opening of haze sanctuaries, particularly for seniors, children and vulnerable families in non-air-conditioned rental flats who may not have access to air purifiers?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sorry, Mr Christopher de Souza, I am moving on.
